annotation_description: Playing basic Island instead of Watery Grave on turn 1 is slightly suboptimal. The hand contains Essence Scatter (1U), Negate (1U), and Requiting Hex (B). Playing Watery Grave (paying 2 life) would give access to both U and B on turn 2 with any second land, enabling both countermagic and Requiting Hex. Playing Island first means if they draw no other blue source, they need to sequence Watery Grave later anyway. More importantly, with Watery Grave turn 1, they can play Island turn 2 and have UU+B available, or play Swamp turn 2 and have UB available. With Island turn 1, playing Swamp turn 2 gives only UB (can cast Requiting Hex or Negate but not Essence Scatter which needs 1U), while Watery Grave turn 2 untapped costs life anyway. The key consideration is that playing Watery Grave now preserves flexibility and the 2 life cost is the same whether paid now or later. Playing Island first is defensible since it avoids the life payment, but with a hand full of reactive spells wanting early mana flexibility, Watery Grave untapped turn 1 is generally better.

Playing Breeding Pool Turn 1 instead of Hushwood Verge limits Turn 2 options. If Breeding Pool enters tapped (correct since nothing to cast T1), then Turn 2 Hushwood Verge only provides G+G, meaning Doc Aurlock (GU) can't be cast Turn 2. Playing Hushwood Verge first, then Breeding Pool Turn 2 (paying 2 life) provides G+GU, enabling the powerful Doc Aurlock on curve.

Playing Swamp instead of Watery Grave (paying 2 life) is suboptimal here. With Island + Swamp, GPT4om has access to UB but cannot cast Negate (which costs 1U - needs two sources including U). With Watery Grave (untapped), they'd have Island + Watery Grave giving them access to UU or UB, enabling both Essence Scatter and Negate on turn 2. Playing Swamp means they can only hold up one of their two-mana counterspells (Essence Scatter with Island+Swamp for 1U works, but Negate also works with 1U). Actually, both Island + Swamp = U + B, which gives 1U for either Essence Scatter or Negate. So the mana works the same for counterspells this turn. However, Watery Grave would be better played now while the opponent has limited pressure, preserving Swamp for a later turn when life total matters more. More importantly, playing Watery Grave now keeps Restless Reef available for later (it enters tapped), and Watery Grave provides more flexible mana (both U and B from one land). The difference is marginal since both lines leave up 1U for counters, but Watery Grave is slightly better for future flexibility.

Playing Doc Aurlock before playing the land from hand is a sequencing error. The player has Hallowed Fountain and Starting Town in hand. They should play a land first (Starting Town enters untapped on turn 2, or Hallowed Fountain paying 2 life) to have more mana available, or at minimum to not miss the land drop if something unexpected happens. More importantly, casting Doc Aurlock into open mana (the opponent has Island + Swamp, exactly enough for Essence Scatter) is risky. While this can't always be avoided with a 2-drop, the player could have played the land first and then cast Badgermole Cub instead, which would earthbend a land and provide mana acceleration - arguably a stronger turn 2 play that also doesn't lose to the legend rule since they have two Doc Aurlocks. However, Doc Aurlock is a reasonable turn 2 play for its cost reduction abilities. The main concrete error is not playing the land before casting the creature.

With 3 lands available (Breeding Pool for G/U, Hushwood Verge for G/W, Hallowed Fountain for W/U), the player could cast Doc Aurlock (GU) or Badgermole Cub (1G) or Airbender Ascension (1W) instead of Llanowar Elves. The opponent has 3 lands with only 2 untapped (Island and Swamp), meaning they likely have Essence Scatter/counter mana available. Playing Llanowar Elves into potential counter mana is less punishing than losing a 2-drop like Doc Aurlock, but the opponent already used Essence Scatter on a previous Doc Aurlock (it's in both graveyards). Playing Llanowar Elves first is a reasonable 'test the waters' play, but the player could have led with Airbender Ascension (a noncreature spell that dodges Essence Scatter) to get value and then followed up with Llanowar Elves. With 1W available after tapping for Airbender Ascension (tap Hushwood Verge for W, Hallowed Fountain for W... no, need 1W = 2 mana). Actually: tap Breeding Pool for G, Hallowed Fountain for W = cast Airbender Ascension for 1W? No, 1W needs one generic + one white. Tap Breeding Pool (G) + Hallowed Fountain (W) = GW, which pays 1W. Then Hushwood Verge is untapped but only produces G (no Forest/Plains in type... wait, Breeding Pool is Forest Island, so Hushwood Verge can tap for W or G). So after casting Airbender Ascension, Hushwood Verge could tap for G to cast Llanowar Elves. This line gets both Airbender Ascension (dodges creature counters) AND Llanowar Elves on the same turn, which is strictly better than just Llanowar Elves alone.

Killing Llanowar Elves with Requiting Hex while Badgermole Cub is on the stack. The Cub is a higher-value target (2/2 body with mana-doubling ability) and also has MV 2, making it a legal Requiting Hex target. The Cub's ETB earthbend triggers regardless, but saving the Hex for the Cub removes the bigger body and the creature-mana-doubling ability.

Feed the Cycle was used to destroy the opponent's earthbent Hallowed Fountain (a 1/1 land creature) instead of the Badgermole Cub (2/2). The Badgermole Cub is a much more significant threat — it provides mana acceleration (extra {G} when tapping creatures for mana) and is an actual creature that can attack. Destroying the Hallowed Fountain only removes a 1/1 body, and when an earthbent land dies, it returns to the battlefield tapped — so the opponent doesn't even permanently lose the land. The Badgermole Cub is permanently destroyed and represents far more board impact.

chosen_display: Demolition Field — {2}, {T}, Sacrifice {this}: Destroy target nonbas... [Activate]
annotation_description: Activating Demolition Field while Feed the Cycle is on the stack prevents playing a land drop first. If they waited for the stack to clear, they could play a land (e.g., Swamp or Watery Grave) before activating Demolition Field, maintaining better mana development. The 2 mana spent on Demolition Field plus the sacrifice means they end with the same number of lands either way, but playing a land first would give them 4 lands post-resolution instead of 3.

Playing Restless Reef (enters tapped) instead of Swamp or Watery Grave (enter untapped) means GPT4om cannot cast Feed the Cycle this turn to kill Badgermole Cub while the opponent is completely tapped out. Badgermole Cub provides ongoing mana advantage and the earthbend ability has already generated value. Missing this removal window while opponent can't respond is a real cost.

Casting Doc Aurlock into an opponent with 4 lands (all tapped currently, but will untap next turn) and a graveyard containing Essence Scatter is risky. The opponent has shown they have countermagic (Essence Scatter already used once) and removal (Requiting Hex). However, since the opponent's lands are all tapped, Doc Aurlock will resolve this turn. The bigger question is sequencing: playing Starting Town first would give access to 5 mana sources next turn and doesn't cost anything. Additionally, casting Doc Aurlock before combat means the opponent sees the board state before blocks matter (though Badgermole Cub is the only attacker anyway). The play of Doc Aurlock is reasonable since it reduces costs for cards cast from graveyard (relevant with Llanowar Elves and Doc Aurlock #1 in graveyard) and the opponent is tapped out. But not playing Starting Town first before casting the spell is a minor sequencing issue - lands should generally be played before spells to preserve information and maximize mana availability.

Opponent is completely tapped out with no blockers available. Attacking with only Badgermole Cub (2 damage) instead of both Badgermole Cub and Doc Aurlock (4 damage total) leaves 2 free damage on the table with zero risk.

chosen_display: Demolition Field — {2}, {T}, Sacrifice {this}: Destroy target nonbas... [Activate]
annotation_description: Activating Demolition Field before playing a land from hand. Libby has Watery Grave and Swamp in hand and hasn't made a land drop this turn. She should play a land first to ensure she has maximum mana available next turn. Additionally, the value of Demolition Field's activation is questionable here since both players replace the destroyed land with a basic, and Libby may need the mana source more than the marginal color disruption against the opponent.

Playing Watery Grave instead of Swamp when there are no blue spells in hand. Swamp provides the same black mana without costing 2 life (if entering untapped) or tempo (if entering tapped). Both lands provide the BB needed for Deadly Cover-Up equally well.

Opponent has no blockers available (Restless Reef is tapped, no creatures) and only 1 untapped mana. Attacking with only Badgermole Cub deals 2 damage when attacking with both Badgermole Cub and Llanowar Elves would deal 3. There's no reason to hold back Llanowar Elves - hand contains only a land, all lands are tapped, and there's nothing to use the Elves' mana for.

Chose Undercity Sewers as one of two picks from Consult the Star Charts when already having sufficient mana (5 lands + Swamp in hand) to cast Deadly Cover-Up. The tapped land provides marginal value while countermagic would be far more impactful for controlling the game after the board wipe.

Playing Undercity Sewers (enters tapped) instead of Swamp (enters untapped) means GPT4om Libby cannot cast Deadly Cover-Up this turn. With Swamp untapped, they'd have 6 mana including the needed {B}{B} (Swamp + existing Swamp + Watery Grave) to board wipe immediately. The opponent has Badgermole Cub, Llanowar Elves, and other threats on board - delaying the wipe by a full turn gives the opponent another turn to develop and attack.

message: Select cards (selected 0 of 2, min 2) (to put into your hand)
annotation_description: GPT4om Libby already has Deadly Cover-Up in hand and picked a second copy from Stock Up instead of the more versatile Three Steps Ahead. Having two 5-mana board wipes is redundant when at 7 life and needing diverse answers. Three Steps Ahead provides countermagic to protect the board wipe or draw cards, covering more situations.

message: Select a card ORDER to put on the BOTTOM of your library (last one chosen will be bottommost)
annotation_description: Chose to draw 2/discard 1 with Three Steps Ahead instead of countering opponent's Stock Up on the stack. Countering Stock Up would deny the opponent +2 cards of card selection, which represents a larger card advantage swing than drawing 2 and discarding 1 (net +1). At 7 life with Deadly Cover-Up already in hand, denying the opponent resources to rebuild after the wipe seems more valuable than digging for cards.

GPT4om Libby used Requiting Hex to destroy Starting Town (a 1/1 animated land) instead of Llanowar Elves (a 1/1 mana dork). Starting Town is an earthbent land - when it dies, it returns to the battlefield tapped as a regular land, so destroying it doesn't actually remove any permanent from the board. The opponent loses the 1/1 body but gets the land back. Destroying Llanowar Elves would permanently remove a mana dork, denying the opponent mana acceleration. Alternatively, Badgermole Cub (mana value 2) is also a valid target and would be a permanent removal of a 2/2 creature body. Given that Libby is at 7 life and needs to reduce the opponent's board pressure, killing the Badgermole Cub (removing a real 2/2 threat permanently) or at minimum the Llanowar Elves (removing mana acceleration permanently) would have been better than killing an animated land that just comes back.

Failed to play Demolition Field before casting Deadly Cover-Up. Playing lands before spells is standard sequencing - the Demolition Field enters untapped and costs nothing, giving an extra land on board for future turns.

When collecting evidence 6 for Deadly Cover-Up, choosing Requiting Hex (MV 1) only brings the total to 5, requiring yet another card to be exiled. Choosing Consult the Star Charts (MV 2) would have reached exactly 6, preserving one more card in the graveyard.

Deadly Cover-Up with evidence collected lets you exile a card from the opponent's graveyard and then search their graveyard, hand, and library for all copies to exile them. Choosing Hallowed Fountain - a land - is nearly worthless since the opponent has no more copies in hand or library that matter strategically. The opponent's graveyard contains key threats like Badgermole Cub (2 copies), Doc Aurlock, Grizzled Genius (2 copies), and Llanowar Elves (2 copies). Exiling Badgermole Cub or Doc Aurlock would strip additional copies from the opponent's hand and library, significantly weakening their future game plan. At 1 life, GPT4om Libby desperately needs to prevent the opponent from rebuilding, and removing a key creature from all zones would be far more impactful than exiling a land.

Cast Deadly Cover-Up when there are zero creatures on the battlefield. While collecting evidence 6 could exile some cards from the opponent's graveyard and search for copies, spending a premium 5-mana board wipe on an empty board wastes a critical answer. At 1 life, holding the wipe for when the opponent actually deploys threats from exile (via Interdimensional Web Watch) is far more important.

With Deadly Cover-Up's evidence ability, chose to exile Badgermole Cub (a modest 2/2 with earthbend) instead of the much more threatening Appa, Steadfast Guardian (3/4 flash flyer that creates tokens) or Doc Aurlock, Grizzled Genius (the engine piece enabling cheap casting from exile). At 1 life, the flash flying threat of Appa is far more dangerous and harder to interact with.

The opponent also gets to search for a basic land, partially negating the effect. Libby's priority should be attacking with Restless Reef to present a clock.
